description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, exercised as the @Service it became (util.DateUtilityJob) and never through a JobLauncher or an HTTP layer: no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc names it, and it is CALLed four times from two online programs - CORPT00C at L392 and L412, COTRN02C at L393 and L413. LS-DATE='2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='QQQQ-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85), each written out to the declared PIC X(10) width so no column is left to a pad; LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no SELECT, opens no file and issues no EXEC CICS, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record, paints no screen and takes no job parameter; its whole observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. This case pins arm 7 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-BAD-PIC-STRING, matched at L141, where L142 moves 'Bad Pic String ' into WS-RESULT PIC X(15) - fourteen characters of text and one trailing space already inside the quotes in the source, so the fifteenth column is the author's own padding and not a pad this fixture applied. Severity and message number are DECODED from that arm's 88-level VALUE X'000309D659C3C5C5' (L68) rather than interpolated: CASE-1-CONDITION-ID (L71-L73) declares SEVERITY PIC S9(4) BINARY then MSG-NO PIC S9(4) BINARY, so the leading halfword 0x0003 is the severity and the second halfword 0x09D6 is 9*256+214 = 2518, while the trailing 59 C3 C5 C5 is the severity-control byte and the facility identifier 'CEE' in EBCDIC and takes no part in the message. Decoding rather than inferring matters because the nine tokens at L62-L70 run 0000, 2507, 2508, 2509, 2513, 2517, 2518, 2520 and 2521 - non-contiguous, skipping 2510-2512, 2514-2516 and 2519 - so no neighbour's number can be guessed from position. The numeric REDEFINES views WS-SEVERITY-N (L44) and WS-MSG-NO-N (L47), written at L123 and L124, therefore render '0003' and '2518' zero-filled to four digits, and RETURN-CODE is 3. Arm 7 is reached here by the UNRECOGNISED-LETTER route: 'Q' begins no recognised picture token, so the PICTURE STRING ITSELF is invalid and is refused at the token lookup, strictly before the input date is examined at all. That is what separates this case from its two siblings on the same arm - in case16 ('YYYY-MM-YY') every character is a legitimate token and the fault is that the YEAR role is declared twice, and in case17 ('<AD-MM-DD ') the era field is opened at the very first character and never closed. Three cases, one arm, three genuinely different paths, which is exactly the collapse a field-for-field diff must be able to see. It is equally distinct from case05 (a wholly blank mask) and case06 ('YYYY      '), which report 2507 FC-INSUFFICIENT-DATA and not 2518: in both of those every position is either a literal delimiter or a legitimate year token, so the picture string is WELL FORMED and merely under-specified, whereas this one is malformed. A blank mask is therefore deliberately NOT this case's input - it belongs to case05, and asserting 2518 for it here would contradict that case while asserting two different outcomes for one identical input. It differs again from case14 ('2022XYZ19 ' under 'YYYYMMMDD '), where the mask parses perfectly and it is the DATE that fails with 2517, and from case18 ('ABCD-EF-GH' under 'YYYY-MM-DD'), which is 2520 FC-NON-NUMERIC-DATA because letters stand where DIGITS were declared beneath a mask that is itself valid. The date here is the good one case01 converts under 'YYYY-MM-DD', which isolates the mask as the sole cause of the failure, and because WS-DATE still reports that date the case also shows the message being assembled from BOTH parameters even when only one of them is at fault. The two X(10) spans of the message behave ASYMMETRICALLY and that asymmetry is load-bearing. WS-DATE at offset 45 is deliberately NOT the date as supplied: L105-L106 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the DECLARED length, hence always 10 - into VSTRING-LENGTH, L107-L108 puts the date into both VSTRING-TEXT and WS-DATE, and L122 then moves the whole WS-DATE-TO-TEST group into WS-DATE PIC X(10), overwriting L107; because that group opens with Vstring-length PIC S9(4) BINARY (L26) the receiver takes the leftmost ten bytes, so the two-byte binary halfword X'000A' survives and only the first eight text bytes '2022-07-' follow it, the trailing '19' truncated on the right. WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is by contrast CLEAN: L111-L113 set it by an ordinary X(10) to X(10) move BEFORE the CALL at L116 and L122 targets WS-DATE alone, so the offending mask is echoed back verbatim - no two-byte prefix, no blanking, and no correction of a mask the program has just rejected. That matters most here because the mask is the faulty parameter: the case shows the invalid picture string reproduced exactly in the message that rejects it. Both behaviours are preserved as observed rather than tidied. The 80-byte geometry is mechanical: the thirteen storage spans declared at L42-L57 sum to 4+11+4+1+15+1+9+10+1+10+10+1+3 = 80, the two numeric REDEFINES overlays contribute none, and INITIALIZE WS-MESSAGE at L90 does not clear FILLER, so the three literals 'Mesg Code:' in an X(11) span (one trailing space), 'TstDate:' in an X(09) span (one trailing space) and 'Mask used:' in an X(10) span (no padding at all) always appear. The line closes with exactly four consecutive spaces - the FILLER at L56 and the three at L57 - because this mask fills all ten of its own columns. Both callers corroborate those offsets independently of WS-MESSAGE by redefining the returned 80 bytes as CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD X(04) + FILLER X(11) + CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM X(04) + CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG X(61), itself summing to 80 (CORPT00C L129-L136, COTRN02C L62-L69), which is where the severity at [0,4) and the message number at [15,19) are read in production. Neither in-repository caller passes this mask - both declare WS-DATE-FORMAT PIC X(10) VALUE 'YYYY-MM-DD' (CORPT00C L72, COTRN02C L60) - so this case exercises the subprogram's own published byte contract beyond the single mask its callers happen to use, which is the contract a CALLed subprogram is obliged to honour. Both would reject this result: each accepts severity '0000' and additionally tolerates only message number '2513' (CORPT00C L396-L399 and L416-L419, COTRN02C L397-L400 and L417-L420), so severity 0003 with 2518 drives 'Start Date - Not a valid date...', 'End Date - Not a valid date...', 'Orig Date - Not a valid date...' and 'Proc Date - Not a valid date...' at the four CALL sites. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl - the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 summed span by span, the nine feedback tokens at L62-L70, the group move at L122 and the EVALUATE at L128-L149 - and were NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the COBOL, which is impossible in this environment: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING at L88 makes this a subprogram the available compiler refuses to build as an executable, and no Language Environment services are reachable, so the CALL "CEEDAYS" at L116 that decides every outcome has no implementation to call and is reproduced by a hand-written total guard chain. Only the provenance of the expectation is substituted; the twenty-case set, the field-by-field diff and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'QQQQ-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
